properties.claim: S2 is a strict additive extension of S1 by relation_lookup_direct.
The matched v0.2 experiment gives S1 and S2 the same persistent relation representation and stored information.
Tested S1 programs preserve result and machine-state contents under S2.
Direct lookup is read-only with respect to machine_data and interpreter store in the current dict-backed fixture.
relation_lookup_direct accepts a Mapping and key, returns the mapped value, and returns NIL for a missing key.
Direct lookup is explicitly charged one access tick; state_read is charged separately.
The direct primitive performs no preprocessing, cache construction, or target-specific representation construction.
S1 and S2 are semantically equivalent on the recorded five-query workload.
S2 changes access to an already-read relation value rather than information availability or target timing.
The one-tick direct access accounting is not evidence of a universal O(1) lookup theorem.
S2 currently depends on host-language Mapping/get semantics.
The current evidence does not establish an absolute computability separation between S2 and S1.

known_gaps: host Mapping semantics are not yet lifted into an explicit object-language relation contract
next_discriminating_action: Reconcile these properties with the canonical Machine interpreter and repeat the matched S1/S2 property suite there.
